chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
"Sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah is [recommended] in all prayers, if there is no prayer performed before the Iqamah."

key_terms.اَلْإِقَامَةِ: The Iqamah (second call to commence prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting between the Adhan and Iqamah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the etiquette of *sukut* (silence) between the Adhan and Iqamah, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s instruction to pray during this interval. The condition regarding the absence of an intervening prayer clarifies that this specific window of merit applies only when the congregation is preparing for the immediate congregational prayer, distinguishing it from voluntary prayers offered in the interim. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maximizing spiritual reward through mindful transitions between the call to prayer and its commencement.
